title: Why Proving War Crimes Is Difficult and Rare

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin, and I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 早在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带着300张你最珍爱的藏品去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 然后你会把DJ台变成这样一个充满生机的、宛如美丽的50年历史文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜欢的播客平台上收听由爱彼表呈献的《重构者》。

sentences.en: I'm Carlotta Gall.
sentences.zh: 我是卡洛塔·加尔。

sentences.en: I reported from Bucha, Ukraine, on Sunday, April the 3rd.
sentences.zh: 我在4月3日星期日从乌克兰布恰进行了报道。

sentences.en: We drove in from the west, and one of the first things you see is along the highway and then at intersections, smashed cars.
sentences.zh: 我们从西边开车进去，你看到的第一批东西之一就是沿着公路以及十字路口处，停放着被砸毁的汽车。

sentences.en: You can't understand how or what happened, but it's chilling because some of them look like they've been pushed aside by tanks or even rolled over.
sentences.zh: 你无法理解是如何发生或发生了什么，但这是令人毛骨悚然的，因为其中一些汽车看起来像是被坦克推开，甚至被压过去了一样。

sentences.en: And so when we got into Bucha, just as we were exploring, and that's what you do when you're a reporter, you drive into a place, you start looking and talking to people.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们进入布恰时，就在我们探索的时候——作为记者你就是这样做的，你开车到一个地方，开始观察并与人们交谈。

sentences.en: And a woman was in great distress, begged us to go to a house where she said a civilian woman had been killed in her garden.
sentences.zh: 有一位女士非常悲痛，恳求我们去一座房子，她说那里有一名平民女性在花园里被杀了。

sentences.en: And so she took us up there, and her elderly mother was there, who was 76, and she described what happened.
sentences.zh: 于是她把我们带了上去，她76岁的老母亲也在那里，并向我们描述了发生的事情。

sentences.en: And she said, a column of tanks, of Russian tanks, drove in down the road.
sentences.zh: 她说，一列坦克，俄罗斯坦克的车队，顺着路开了进来。

sentences.en: You know, her daughter ran out into the garden saying, they're ours, they're our troops.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她的女儿跑到花园里说，是我们的军队，是我们的部队。

sentences.en: And they immediately opened fire on her.
sentences.zh: 而他们立刻向她开火。

sentences.en: We saw the bullets in her fence, and her daughter died in the garden right there.
sentences.zh: 我们在她家的栅栏上看到了弹孔，她的女儿当时就死在了花园里。

sentences.en: And then this poor woman didn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 然后这个可怜的女人不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: She was shooting and shelling, you know, for days.
sentences.zh: 你知道，枪击和炮击持续了好几天。

sentences.en: And so she half buried her daughter by covering her in plastic sheeting and then covering her with wooden boards.
sentences.zh: 因此，她用塑料布盖住女儿，然后用木板盖上，以此将女儿半埋了。

sentences.en: And she took us into the garden and showed us where her daughter lay, and you could see her feet still in her sort of patterned socks and galoshes poking out under the boards.
sentences.zh: 她把我们带进花园，给我们看了她女儿躺着的地方，你可以看到她的脚还穿着某种带图案的袜子和套鞋，从木板底下伸出来。

sentences.en: So that was one of the first things that happened to us when we drove into Bucha on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 所以，那是我们周日开车进入布恰时遇到的第一件事情之一。

sentences.en: I'm Andrew Kramer.
sentences.zh: 我是安德鲁·克雷默。

sentences.en: I cover Ukraine for The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》报道乌克兰新闻。

sentences.en: When I got to Bucha over the weekend, I didn't know what I would find.
sentences.zh: 当我在周末到达布恰时，我不知道我会发现什么。

sentences.en: And as we were driving down the road, we began to see bodies on the road.
sentences.zh: 当我们沿着道路开车时，我们开始看到路上的尸体。

sentences.en: First, it was one man lying face down on the street.
sentences.zh: 首先是一个面朝下躺在街上的男人。

sentences.en: Another man shot in the head.
sentences.zh: 另一个男人头部中枪。

sentences.en: I ended up talking to the town's coroner.
sentences.zh: 我最后采访了该镇的验尸官。

sentences.en: And he's found so many bodies that he dug a mass grave in a churchyard.
sentences.zh: 他发现了如此多的尸体，以至于他在一个教堂的庭院里挖了一个万人坑。

sentences.en: And even on the day when we met, he had found 13 bodies with their hands tied and shot in the head in an execution.
sentences.zh: 就在我们见面的那天，他还发现了13具双手被反绑、头部中枪、遭到处决的尸体。

sentences.en: He showed me a video on his cell phone of the scene of five bodies lined up kneeling against the wall of the basement with their hands bound behind them.
sentences.zh: 他在手机上给我看了一段视频，现场有五具尸体双手反绑在身后，跪着排成一排靠在地下室的墙上。

sentences.en: In all my conversations with people in Bucha, it was clear that whatever an international court might decide, certainly the people living there.
sentences.zh: 在我与布恰居民所有的交谈中，很明显，无论国际法庭可能作出什么裁决，对于生活在那里的人们来说……

sentences.en: And when they thought about their loved ones, their friends, their relatives, who had been murdered and were still lying on the streets, they were saying that, in their view,
sentences.zh: 当他们想到自己那些被谋杀、至今仍躺在街上的至亲、朋友和亲戚时，他们说，在他们看来，

sentences.en: these were war crimes.
sentences.zh: 这些都是战争罪行。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: As global outrage grows over Russian atrocities in the town of Bucha, a number of world leaders, like residents, are calling what happened there a war crime.
sentences.zh: 随着国际社会对俄罗斯在布恰镇暴行的愤怒不断加剧，许多世界领导人和当地居民一样，将那里发生的事情称为战争罪。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Roger Cohen, explains that proving such crimes is both difficult and rare.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事罗杰·科恩解释说，证明此类罪行既困难又罕见。

sentences.en: I spoke to him about one of the very few cases where it worked.
sentences.zh: 我曾就一个极少数成功的案例跟他谈过。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, April 6th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月6日，星期三。

sentences.en: Roger, tell me what went through your mind when you first saw those images out of Bucha over the weekend.
sentences.zh: 罗杰，能告诉我你周末刚看到布查那些画面时，心里是怎么想的吗？

sentences.en: Well, it was the horror of it that struck me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最让我震撼的是那种恐怖感。

sentences.en: And I hate to say it, but in a way, the familiarity.
sentences.zh: 而且我讨厌这么说，但在某种程度上，还有那种熟悉感。

sentences.en: If you've covered wars, as I have, atrocities tend to happen.
sentences.zh: 如果你像我一样报道过战争，暴行往往是会发生的。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, seeing these victims in Bucha, apparently summarily executed and apparently by the Russian occupying army, well, it sent a shiver through me.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，看到布查的这些受害者，显然是被就地正法，而且显然是俄罗斯占领军干的，这确实让我不寒而栗。

sentences.en: This looked on the face of it very much like war crimes.
sentences.zh: 从表面上看，这非常像是战争罪。

sentences.en: And when you say it's a war crime, what are the rules of engagement specifically that kind of define that?
sentences.zh: 当你说这是一场战争罪时，具体是哪些交战规则界定了这一点？

sentences.en: Well, Sabrina, international law, as compiled, put together, defined, requires that the parties to a conflict distinguish between competence and non-competence,
sentences.zh: 好吧，萨布丽娜，已汇编、整合并界定的国际法要求冲突各方区分战斗人员与非战斗人员，

sentences.en: between competence and civilians.
sentences.zh: 区分战斗人员与平民。

sentences.en: And it is a war crime to intentionally target civilians or places where civilians might well be, including hospitals, schools, houses, places of worship.
sentences.zh: 蓄意攻击平民或平民可能聚集的场所（包括医院、学校、住宅和礼拜场所）属于战争罪。

sentences.en: And that kind of indiscriminate attack on civilians can constitute a war crime.
sentences.zh: 对平民进行这种无差别的攻击可以构成战争罪。

sentences.en: On the face of it, it does.
sentences.zh: 表面上看，确实如此。

sentences.en: And when did these ideas become international norms?
sentences.zh: 这些理念是什么时候成为国际准则的？

sentences.en: I mean, how did the world agree on these definitions?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，世界是如何就这些定义达成一致的？

sentences.en: Well, slowly and painfully, what happened was that after World War II, a decision was taken to hold two international trials.
sentences.zh: 嗯，过程缓慢而痛苦，情况是这样的：第二次世界大战后，各方决定进行两场国际审判。

sentences.en: This is the building in Nuremberg where 20 top Nazis are being tried for many crimes.
sentences.zh: 这就是纽伦堡的那栋大楼，20名纳粹高官正在那里因多项罪行受审。

sentences.en: One in Nuremberg, the principal one, and another also in Tokyo.
sentences.zh: 一场在纽伦堡，即主要的审判，另一场则在东京。

sentences.en: Twenty-eight Japanese war criminals, including former Premier Hideki Tojo, go on trial in Tokyo to answer for the aggressive cruelty which they sponsored.
sentences.zh: 包括前首相东条英机在内的二十八名日本战犯在东京受审，为他们纵容的侵略残暴行径承担责任。

sentences.en: And the prisoners are charged with crimes against humanity and peace.
sentences.zh: 囚犯们被指控犯有反人类罪和危害和平罪。

sentences.en: And in these trials, some new concepts were introduced, particularly the idea of a crime against humanity,
sentences.zh: 在这些审判中，引入了一些新概念，特别是反人类罪的思想，

sentences.en: a crime against humanity being the intentional targeting of a particular group of people, of civilians, in order to eliminate them.
sentences.zh: 反人类罪是指为了消灭特定的一群人或平民而蓄意将其作为目标。

sentences.en: So these trials were held, and they resulted in convictions in many cases.
sentences.zh: 因此举行了这些审判，在许多情况下，审判结果是定罪。

sentences.en: And that was really the beginning of the serious thought about setting down international rules, laws.
sentences.zh: 这确实是开始认真思考制定国际规则和法律的开端。

sentences.en: But what you had, in essence, was a very, very long pause of about a half century,
sentences.zh: 但本质上，你经历了一段非常非常漫长、大约半个世纪的停滞，

sentences.en: during which no international criminal court or international tribunal was set up that could prosecute anyone using this new range of laws that had emerged from the horrors and the Holocaust of World War II.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，没有建立任何国际刑事法院或国际法庭，能够利用第二次世界大战的恐怖和大屠杀中涌现出的这一系列新法律来起诉任何人。

sentences.en: So, in essence, during the Cold War, you just had a big gap, a big vacuum, during which, having established the laws, nobody seemed prepared to act on them.
sentences.zh: 所以，从本质上讲，在冷战期间，你只有一个巨大的缺口、巨大的真空，在此期间，尽管法律已经确立，但似乎没有人准备据此采取行动。

sentences.en: So, essentially, back in the 40s, the laws were established.
sentences.zh: 因此，基本上在20世纪40年代，法律就已经确立了。

sentences.en: There was this long period where no one really used them.
sentences.zh: 经历了一段很长的时期，没有人真正使用它们。

sentences.en: And then what happened?
sentences.zh: 然后发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, then the Cold War ended and felt like the outbreak of peace across the world.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后冷战结束了，感觉就像全世界爆发了和平。

sentences.en: But, in fact, the most terrible fighting in Europe since World War II broke out pretty quickly with the breakup of the former Yugoslavia.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，随着前南斯拉夫的解体，欧洲自二战以来最可怕的战斗相当快地爆发了。

sentences.en: Yugoslavia, much like the Soviet Union, broke up after the fall of communism.
sentences.zh: 南斯拉夫很像苏联，在共产主义倒台后解体了。

sentences.en: And in that breakup, terrible wars broke out that lasted for four and a half years.
sentences.zh: 在那场解体中，爆发了持续四年半的可怕战争。

sentences.en: There was a genocide in Bosnia.
sentences.zh: 波斯尼亚发生了种族灭绝。

sentences.en: So, for the first time, all these rules that came into being in the 1940s were actually going to be tested.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些在20世纪40年代诞生的规则将首次真正接受检验。

sentences.en: Now, it's very complicated.
sentences.zh: 现在，情况非常复杂。

sentences.en: We look at a body in Bucha with a Ukrainian man, a woman, with his or her hands bound, and we think, well, clearly there's been a crime.
sentences.zh: 我们和一位乌克兰男女同胞一起在布查查看一具尸体，他的双手被反绑着，我们想，好吧，这显然是一起犯罪。

sentences.en: But to get the evidence, to bring a defendant to court, to go through all the investigation is painstakingly difficult.
sentences.zh: 但要收集证据、将被告送上法庭并完成所有调查，是极其困难的。

sentences.en: It is a very slow, painful process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常缓慢、痛苦的过程。

sentences.en: That's been the lesson of the last 20, 30 years that came out of the Bosnian trials.
sentences.zh: 这是波斯尼亚审判得出的过去20、30年的教训。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, how did it work in Bosnia?
sentences.zh: 那么，波斯尼亚的情况是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: So, much like with the breakup of the Soviet Union, when Yugoslavia broke up in 1992, its constituent republics went their own way as independent states,
sentences.zh: 就像苏联解体一样，1992年南斯拉夫解体时，其组成共和国作为独立国家走上了各自的道路，

sentences.en: much like Ukraine or Kazakhstan went their own way from the Soviet Union and became independent.
sentences.zh: 就像乌克兰或哈萨克斯坦脱离苏联走上各自的道路并独立一样。

sentences.en: The problem for the leader of Serbia, Slobodan Milosevic, is that in one of these newly independent states, Bosnia, 40% or 35% was made up of ethnic Serbs.
sentences.zh: 塞尔维亚领导人斯洛博丹·米洛舍维奇面临的问题是，在这些新独立的国家之一波斯尼亚，有40%或35%的人口是族裔塞尔维亚人。

sentences.en: And Milosevic held absolutely that these ethnic Serbs should not be taken out of Serbia, that Serbia should extend as far as there was any Serb.
sentences.zh: 米洛舍维奇坚信，这些族裔塞尔维亚人不应该被剥离出塞尔维亚，塞尔维亚的领土应该延伸到有塞尔维亚人存在的任何地方。

sentences.en: Much like President Putin from very early in the 90s was feeling deeply aggrieved that 25 million ethnic Russians or Russian speakers had ended up outside the Russia that was born at the collapse of the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 就像普京总统从90年代初开始就深感委屈，因为有2500万族裔俄罗斯人或俄语人口最终落在了苏联解体时诞生的俄罗斯国境之外。

sentences.en: Okay, so this is a guy who, as you said, very much like Putin, sees this collapsing state and sees his people, ethnic Serbs who are Christians, scattered around it,
sentences.zh: 好的，所以这是一个正如你所说、非常像普京的人，他看到这个崩溃的国家，看到他的子民——作为基督徒的族裔塞尔维亚人——散落其间，

sentences.en: and wants to claim rights and territory on their behalf, in this case in Bosnia.
sentences.zh: 并想要代表他们声索权利和领土，在这个案例中就是波斯尼亚。

sentences.en: So, what does Milosevic do?
sentences.zh: 那么，米洛舍维奇做了什么？

sentences.en: Unlike President Putin, who waited some years to annex territory and ultimately invade Ukraine, President Milosevic did not wait at all.
sentences.zh: 与等待了几年才吞并领土并最终入侵乌克兰的普京总统不同，米洛舍维奇总统一点也没有等。

sentences.en: He went to war the day that Bosnian independence was recognized in 1992, and he set out to ethnically cleanse wide areas of Bosnia.
sentences.zh: 他在1992年波斯尼亚独立被承认的那天就发动了战争，并着手对波斯尼亚的大片地区进行种族清洗。

sentences.en: That's to say, remove any non-Serb population.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，清除任何非塞尔维亚人口。

sentences.en: And his idea was that thereby he could extend Serbia to become greater Serbia, while at the same time effectively destroying Bosnia at its birth.
sentences.zh: 他的想法是，以此将塞尔维亚扩展为大塞尔维亚，同时在波斯尼亚诞生之初就彻底摧毁它。

sentences.en: I went into Bosnia for the first time in 1992, a few months after the war began.
sentences.zh: 我于1992年第一次进入波斯尼亚，那是战争爆发几个月后。

sentences.en: I was asked to go cover the war, and it was one of the craziest scenes I'd ever witnessed.
sentences.zh: 我被要求去报道这场战争，这是我见过的最疯狂的场景之一。

sentences.en: What did you see?
sentences.zh: 你看到了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I went in on a bus from Belgrade, and everyone on this bus was giddy with Milosevic's wild nationalism and visions of Serbs avenging past wrongs against them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我坐着从贝尔格莱德来的巴士进去，车上的每个人都沉浸在米洛舍维奇疯狂的民族主义以及塞尔维亚人要报复过去对他们的不公的幻觉中，兴奋不已。

sentences.en: And they were singing, and they were drinking, and as soon as we got to the Bosnian borders, somebody got onto the bus and handed out automatic rifles to everyone on the bus.
sentences.zh: 他们又唱又喝，一到波斯尼亚边界，就有人上了车，给车上的每个人分发了自动步枪。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And on we went into this crazy war.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就这样进入了这场疯狂的战争。

sentences.en: We went to the Bosnian Serbs' so-called capital, a place called Pale, P-A-L-E.
sentences.zh: 我们去了波斯尼亚塞尔维亚人所谓的首都，一个叫帕莱的地方，P-A-L-E。

sentences.en: And then from there, you know, Sarajevo is the capital of Bosnia.
sentences.zh: 然后从那里，你知道的，萨拉热窝是波斯尼亚的首都。

sentences.en: The Sarajevo Winter Olympics had been held only a few years earlier.
sentences.zh: 萨拉热窝冬季奥运会仅仅在几年前举行过。

sentences.en: It's a mountainous area, and we went to the mountains overlooking Sarajevo.
sentences.zh: 那是一个多山地区，我们去了俯瞰萨拉热窝的山区。

sentences.en: And I was taken to positions where Serbian artillery was firing shells down onto the city.
sentences.zh: 我被带到了塞尔维亚炮兵向城内开火的阵地。

sentences.en: Now, you remember what we said about war crimes and the indiscriminate targeting of civilians.
sentences.zh: 现在，还记得我们关于战争罪和无差别针对平民的言论吗？

sentences.en: This was not an attempt of any kind to hit any sort of military target.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是为了打击任何类型的军事目标。

sentences.en: It was simply an attempt to terrorize the Bosnian Muslim population of Sarajevo.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是为了恐吓萨拉热窝的波斯尼亚穆斯林人口。

sentences.en: So at the same time as I was witnessing this indiscriminate Serbian shelling of Sarajevo, in other parts of Bosnia during that summer of 1992, it was far worse.
sentences.zh: 因此，就在我目睹塞尔维亚人对萨拉热窝进行无差别炮击的同时，在1992年那个夏天的波斯尼亚其他地方，情况要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: Tens of thousands of these Bosnian Muslims who had been hounded out of their homes
sentences.zh: 成千上万被赶出家园的波斯尼亚穆斯林

sentences.en: were processed through a series of Serb concentration camps gathered around northern and western Bosnia.
sentences.zh: 被集中穿过聚集在波斯尼亚北部和西部的塞尔维亚人集中营。

sentences.en: Now, there was a great deal of outrage when news of these Serbian-run camps filled it out.
sentences.zh: 当时，当这些由塞尔维亚人运营的集中营的消息传开时，引起了极大的愤怒。

sentences.en: But there was no real reaction from the West or anybody else until 1995, three years later,
sentences.zh: 但直到1995年，也就是三年后，西方或其他任何人都没有做出真正的反应，

sentences.en: when the Serbs perpetrated a single crime that finally convinced the world that something had to be done.
sentences.zh: 当时塞尔维亚人犯下了一起单一罪行，最终让世界确信必须采取行动。

sentences.en: What was that crime?
sentences.zh: 那是什么罪行？

sentences.en: That crime has a name.
sentences.zh: 那个罪行有一个名字。

sentences.en: Its name is Srebrenica.
sentences.zh: 它的名字叫斯雷布雷尼察。

sentences.en: Srebrenica is a small town in eastern Bosnia where, unlike almost all the towns around it in that part of the country,
sentences.zh: 斯雷布雷尼察是波斯尼亚东部的一个小镇，与该国该地区几乎所有周围的小镇不同，

sentences.en: the Bosnian Muslim population had hung on through three and a half years of war until 1995.
sentences.zh: 波斯尼亚穆斯林人口在那里经历了三年半的战争，一直坚持到了1995年。

sentences.en: The Serbs decided, enough already.
sentences.zh: 塞尔维亚人决定，够了。

sentences.en: We're done with Srebrenica.
sentences.zh: 我们受够斯雷布雷尼察了。

sentences.en: It's a little island in the middle of this greater Serbia we're establishing, and we need this population to go.
sentences.zh: 它是我们正在建立的大塞尔维亚中间的一个小岛，我们需要这群人离开。

sentences.en: 8,000 Bosnian Muslim men and boys were summarily executed.
sentences.zh: 8000名波斯尼亚穆斯林男性和男孩被仓决处决。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And the women and some of the children were pushed across the lines, mainly to a town called Tuzla,
sentences.zh: 妇女和一些儿童被驱赶过边界，主要去了一个叫图兹拉的小镇，

sentences.en: where I witnessed in the summer of 1995 these people arriving in the most desperate states, wailing, talking about what had happened to their husbands, to their sons,
sentences.zh: 我在1995年夏天在那里目睹了这些人以极其绝望的状态抵达，痛哭流涕，诉说着他们的丈夫和儿子遭遇了什么，

sentences.en: pleading with us journalists, or indeed anybody, to try to help, to find them.
sentences.zh: 恳求我们记者，或者任何其他人，设法提供帮助，找到他们。

sentences.en: It was an absolutely desperate situation.
sentences.zh: 那是一个绝对绝望的处境。

sentences.en: And when I think back to that bus ride three and a half years earlier, this was the end point of that madness.
sentences.zh: 每当我回想起三年半前的那个巴士之旅，这就是那场疯狂的终点。

sentences.en: And what did that do to the international community?
sentences.zh: 这对国际社会产生了什么影响？

sentences.en: Well, it finally galvanized the international community, and particularly the Clinton administration, to act.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它最终促使国际社会，特别是克林顿政府采取行动。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: I am very disturbed about what has happened in Srebrenica.
sentences.zh: 我对斯雷布雷尼察发生的事情深感不安。

sentences.en: We are very concerned about the fate of the refugees, and we have been working hard for the last couple of days
sentences.zh: 我们非常关注难民的命运，过去几天我们一直在努力工作，

sentences.en: to determine what options there are to deal with the immediate humanitarian probleMs.
sentences.zh: 以确定有哪些方案来解决紧迫的人道主义问题。

sentences.en: And we intend to do everything we can on that.
sentences.zh: 我们打算为此尽我们所能。

sentences.en: At last, a decision was taken to use military force, and airstrikes by NATO were finally ordered on various Serb positions.
sentences.zh: 终于，人们做出了使用军事力量的决定，北约的空袭最终被下令针对塞尔维亚人的各个阵地。

sentences.en: And as a result of this, within days,
sentences.zh: 作为结果，在几天之内，

sentences.en: Slobodan Milosevic, the Serbian leader, folded.
sentences.zh: 塞尔维亚领导人斯洛博丹·米洛舍维奇屈服了。

sentences.en: However, the story was far from over.
sentences.zh: 然而，故事远未结束。

sentences.en: Milosevic was still in power in Belgrade.
sentences.zh: 米洛舍维奇仍然在贝尔格莱德当权。

sentences.en: And increasingly, the Western world felt that he had to be brought to justice.
sentences.zh: 西方世界愈发觉得必须将他绳之以法。

sentences.en: He had to stand trial in an international court for crimes against humanity and for genocide.
sentences.zh: 他必须在国际法庭上因反人类罪和种族灭绝罪接受审判。

sentences.en: It would, however, be a long road to that day.
sentences.zh: 然而，通往那一天的道路还很漫长。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报 Dealbook 报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 Dealbook 峰会上现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些未经排练、未经删减的实时对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选访谈，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约 Times》应用程序进行观看，并免费阅读我们所有的报道一个月。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Roger, you said it was a long road to get to the actual trial of Milosevic.
sentences.zh: 罗杰，你说过，真正把米洛舍维奇送上审判台经历了一段漫长的过程。

sentences.en: Tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲那是怎么回事。

sentences.en: What did they do?
sentences.zh: 他们做了什么？

sentences.en: How did they build the case?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何构建案件的？

sentences.en: Well, it was extremely complicated and on multiple levels.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个过程极其复杂，涉及多个层面。

sentences.en: When the war ended in Bosnia, it was 1995.
sentences.zh: 波黑战争结束时，已经是1995年了。

sentences.en: Milosevic remained in power until the year 2000.
sentences.zh: 米洛舍维奇一直掌权到2000年。

sentences.en: The possibility of extraditing him for trial before an international criminal court in The Hague until he was out of power was pretty much impossible.
sentences.zh: 在他下台之前，把他引渡到海牙的国际刑事法庭受审几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: Then there was the whole question of how to prosecute him.
sentences.zh: 然后还有如何起诉他的整个问题。

sentences.en: Milosevic had never himself set foot in Bosnia.
sentences.zh: 米洛舍维奇本人从未踏足过波黑。

sentences.en: How did you establish a chain of command running up to him from the commanders in the field in Bosnia?
sentences.zh: 你们是如何建立起一条从波黑前线指挥官一直延伸到他的指挥链的？

sentences.en: How did you find the witnesses that were needed to make the case?
sentences.zh: 你们是如何找到破案所需的证人的？

sentences.en: In the end, there would be almost 300 witnesses used against him.
sentences.zh: 最终，将有近300名证人出庭指证他。

sentences.en: So all this took an enormous amount of time, and it was extremely complicated.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切花费了大量的时间，而且极其复杂。

sentences.en: Roger, you said there were around 300 witness interviews.
sentences.zh: 罗杰，你刚才说大约有300名证人访谈。

sentences.en: What were investigators looking for in these interviews?
sentences.zh: 调查人员在这些访谈中寻找什么？

sentences.en: Well, they were looking for people who could testify to war crimes who had been processed through those concentration camps, for example,
sentences.zh: 嗯，例如，他们在寻找能够证明战争罪行的人，他们曾被关押在那些集中营里，

sentences.en: who had been in Srebrenica and had seen what had happened there.
sentences.zh: 去过斯雷布雷尼察并亲眼目睹了那里发生的事情。

sentences.en: People who could, in some way, establish the link between Milosevic and orders that were given in Bosnia.
sentences.zh: 能够以某种方式建立米洛舍维奇与在波黑下达的命令之间联系的人。

sentences.en: The net was cast very wide.
sentences.zh: 网撒得很宽。

sentences.en: I, myself, at one point, was questioned by an investigator from The Hague.
sentences.zh: 有一次，我本人也接受了一名海牙调查人员的盘问。

sentences.en: What kind of questions did the prosecutor ask you, Roger?
sentences.zh: 检察官问了你什么样的问题，罗杰？

sentences.en: Well, it was relating to one of those camps, and it was a camp that I had found that had been unknown until that point, a camp in the eastern part of Bosnia by the name of Susica.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这与其中一个集中营有关，那是我发现的一个此前不为人知的集中营，位于波黑东部，名叫苏西卡（Susica）。

sentences.en: And I was approached by a Serbian commander who had been present at the camp and whose conscience had stirred and had witnessed some of these crimes.
sentences.zh: 有一位曾在该集中营在场、良心发现并目睹了其中一些罪行的塞尔维亚指挥官找到了我。

sentences.en: So the court was interested in reaching this perpetrator and establishing the chain of command up from him to whomever had told him to do what he did.
sentences.zh: 所以法庭有兴趣找到这个犯罪分子，并建立从他到任何指使他做那些事的人的指挥链。

sentences.en: So I think this was the case in many of the interviews.
sentences.zh: 所以我想许多访谈都是这种情况。

sentences.en: It was piece by piece, moment by moment, specific crime by specific crime.
sentences.zh: 这是一个细节接一个细节，时刻接时刻，具体罪行对具体罪行。

sentences.en: So it was a huge undertaking.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一项巨大的工程。

sentences.en: And, Roger, how long did it take for investigators to amass the evidence that they needed to bring charges against Milosevic?
sentences.zh: 罗杰，调查人员花了多长时间才搜集到起诉米洛舍维奇所需的证据？

sentences.en: Well, it took five, six years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，花了两三年……不对，五、六年。

sentences.en: It wasn't until the early 2000s that he was finally brought to the court and charged with these numerous counts of genocide,
sentences.zh: 直到2001年左右，他才最终被带上法庭，并被指控犯有数十项种族灭绝罪，

sentences.en: complicity in genocide, murder, persecution on political, racial, or religious grounds.
sentences.zh: 共谋灭绝种族、谋杀、基于政治、种族或宗教理由的迫害。

sentences.en: I mean, the list goes on.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，名单还在继续。

sentences.en: So it takes five or six years to get Milosevic to a trial for a crime that in a lot of ways seemed very obvious on its face, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，要让米洛舍维奇因一项在很多方面表面上看起来非常明显的罪行接受审判，却花了五六年时间，对吧？

sentences.en: The death and execution of thousands of Muslim men in Bosnia.
sentences.zh: 数千名波黑穆斯林男子的死亡和处决。

sentences.en: Yeah, Milosevic was still in power.
sentences.zh: 是的，米洛舍维奇当时仍然在台下……哦不，在台上。

sentences.en: He was still in power for five years after the end of the Bosnian War.
sentences.zh: 在波黑战争结束后，他仍然掌权了五年。

sentences.en: In 2000, Milosevic was ousted, but he's still living in a country called Serbia.
sentences.zh: 2000年，米洛舍维奇被赶下台，但他仍然生活在一个叫塞尔维亚的国家里。

sentences.en: Now, here, European politics come in, in that Serbia, like the other countries in the Balkans, had this target of one day getting into the EU.
sentences.zh: 现在，这里的欧洲政治介入了，因为塞尔维亚和巴尔干地区的其他国家一样，有一个终极目标，那就是有一天加入欧盟。

sentences.en: No way that was ever going to happen if Milosevic was not extradited.
sentences.zh: 如果米洛舍维奇不被引渡，这是绝对不可能发生的。

sentences.en: So, finally, about a year after he was ousted from power, Milosevic was extradited to The Hague.
sentences.zh: 所以，最终在他被赶下台大约一年后，米洛舍维奇被引渡到了海牙。

sentences.en: But in a way, it sounds like his extradition is really a kind of almost accident.
sentences.zh: 但从某种意义上说，听起来他的引渡其实有点像是偶然。

sentences.en: I mean, it required him losing an election, and it required his country to kind of be looking toward the EU and potential membership to be willing to give him up.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这需要他输掉选举，并且需要他的国家着眼于欧盟和潜在的成员国身份，才愿意放弃他。

sentences.en: Yeah, it required those two things.
sentences.zh: 是的，这需要这两件事。

sentences.en: It required a political change in Serbia, a fairly radical political change.
sentences.zh: 这需要塞尔维亚发生政治变革，一场相当激进的政治变革。

sentences.en: Now, that change did happen.
sentences.zh: 现在，这种变化确实发生了。

sentences.en: And as a result of that, this court that had been set up eight years earlier
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，这个在八年前建立的法庭

sentences.en: finally had the former leader of Serbia in the courtroom.
sentences.zh: 终于迎来了塞尔维亚前领导人出庭受审。

sentences.en: And so these proceedings began.
sentences.zh: 于是这些诉讼程序就开始了。

sentences.en: They were supposed to last no more than two years.
sentences.zh: 它们本应持续不超过两年。

sentences.en: That proved to be a pipe dream.
sentences.zh: 事实证明这只是白日梦。

sentences.en: How long did they last?
sentences.zh: 它们持续了多久？

sentences.en: It lasted four years.
sentences.zh: 持续了四年。

sentences.en: But it didn't end after four years with a conviction.
sentences.zh: 但这四年并没有以定罪告终。

sentences.en: It ended after four years because Slobodan Milosevic died in his cell.
sentences.zh: 这四年结束是因为斯洛博丹·米洛舍维奇死在了牢房里。

sentences.en: He had a heart attack.
sentences.zh: 他突发心脏病。

sentences.en: And as a result, the conclusion to the whole proceedings was unsatisfactory in that Milosevic died during his trial.
sentences.zh: 结果，整个诉讼程序的结局令人很不满意，因为米洛舍维奇在审判期间死了。

sentences.en: However, this was not by any means the end of the matter because in 2011, the military commander in Bosnia, who had been present in Srebrenica,
sentences.zh: 然而，这绝不是事情的结束，因为在2011年，曾在斯雷布雷尼察在场的波黑军事指挥官，

sentences.en: General Ratko Mladic, was finally brought to trial in the same court in the Hague.
sentences.zh: 拉特科·姆拉迪奇将军终于在海牙的同一法庭接受审判。

sentences.en: And he, after six years, was convicted of genocide and other crimes.
sentences.zh: 六年后的他，因犯有种族灭绝和其他罪行而被定罪。

sentences.en: So we're now talking 2017, 22 years after the end of the war in Bosnia.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在说的是2017年，距离波黑战争结束已经过去22年了。

sentences.en: So there were convictions.
sentences.zh: 所以确实有了定罪。

sentences.en: In Milosevic's case, justice was not carried out to the full simply because he died.
sentences.zh: 就米洛舍维奇而言，正义并未得到彻底伸张，仅仅是因为他死了。

sentences.en: Roger, I guess thinking of the story you just told me, it makes me wonder whether these calls for war crimes investigations right now in Ukraine will actually amount to anything.
sentences.zh: 罗杰，我想回想你刚刚讲的故事，这让我怀疑现在在乌克兰对战争罪行调查的呼吁是否真的能有什么结果。

sentences.en: I mean, you have Putin, the leader of Russia, who's not going away anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，俄罗斯领导人普京并不会很快下台。

sentences.en: It's very unlikely there'd be a change of power there.
sentences.zh: 那里发生权力更迭的可能性非常小。

sentences.en: And even if there were, it's even more unlikely that a new government there would, you know, extradite him, would give him up to the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 即便发生了，那里的新政府“你知道的”引渡他、把他交给西方的可能性就更小了。

sentences.en: I guess I'm left with this question of, is this going to mean anything?
sentences.zh: 我想我脑海中留下了这样一个问题：这一切会有意义吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think it means something in the sense that it sets down a marker.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为它在树立一个风向标的意义上是有意义的。

sentences.en: The President of the United States calls Putin a war criminal.
sentences.zh: 美国总统称普京为战犯。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean, obviously, that he's been convicted of such a crime.
sentences.zh: 这显然并不意味着他已经被裁定犯有此类罪行。

sentences.en: But it brings, in a very forcible way, attention to the fact of the horror of what has been perpetrated.
sentences.zh: 但这以一种非常有力度的方式，让人注意到所犯下罪行的恐怖之处。

sentences.en: Now, the distance from that horror, wherever it may be in Ukraine, to a conviction is, as we've been discussing, a long one.
sentences.zh: 正如我们一直在讨论的那样，从乌克兰某处的这种恐怖事件到最终定罪，还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: But if the label war criminal sticks to Putin, he's going to be very limited in the places he's able to go because of the web of extradition relationships
sentences.zh: 但如果“战犯”这个标签贴在普京身上，由于各国之间存在引渡网络，

sentences.en: that exists between many countries.
sentences.zh: 许多国家之间都存在这种网络，

sentences.en: Meaning he'd be stuck in Russia.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他将被困在俄罗斯。

sentences.en: Yeah, if he leaves Russia, and especially if he leaves Russia once he's no longer a head of state.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果他离开俄罗斯，尤其是当他不再是国家元首之后离开俄罗斯。

sentences.en: At some point, he will no longer be head of state.
sentences.zh: 在某个时候，他将不再是国家元首。

sentences.en: One has to assume.
sentences.zh: 人们不得不这样认为。

sentences.en: So I don't think, even if it's cumbersome, even if it's long, even if it's difficult,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，即使它很繁琐，即使它很漫长，即使它很困难，

sentences.en: I don't think that it's pointless.
sentences.zh: 我也不认为这是毫无意义的。

sentences.en: On the contrary, if we simply throw up our hands and say, it's just too difficult, it's just too complicated, look at Bosnia, it took two decades,
sentences.zh: 恰恰相反，如果我们轻易地双手一摊，说这太难了，这太复杂了，看看波斯尼亚，那花了两十年时间，

sentences.en: then we'd simply offer impunity for war crimes.
sentences.zh: 那么我们就是在为战争罪行提供有罪不罚的庇护。

sentences.en: Roger, what's the lesson of Bosnia?
sentences.zh: 罗杰，波斯尼亚给我们的教训是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the lesson of Bosnia, as of Ukraine, is that the unthinkable can happen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如乌克兰一样，波斯尼亚给我们的教训是，不可想象的事情是可能发生的。

sentences.en: Europe was lulled at the time of Bosnia into thinking that war had been banished from the continent.
sentences.zh: 在波斯尼亚事件发生时，欧洲曾陷入一种虚假的安全感，以为战争已经从这片大陆上被驱逐。

sentences.en: And certainly since then, it was lulled into that same state of amnesia.
sentences.zh: 而且肯定的是，从那以后，它一直陷入那种同样的健忘状态。

sentences.en: Peace, however, in terms of the sweep of history, is an exceptional state.
sentences.zh: 然而，从历史的长河来看，和平是一种特殊状态。

sentences.en: It's an unusual state.
sentences.zh: 这是一种不寻常的状态。

sentences.en: And it takes great effort to preserve it.
sentences.zh: 需要付出巨大的努力才能维护它。

sentences.en: The people who were killing each other in Bosnia until they started killing each other were neighbors.
sentences.zh: 在波斯尼亚互相杀戮的人们，在他们开始互相杀戮之前，曾经是邻居。

sentences.en: They lived side by side.
sentences.zh: 他们比邻而居。

sentences.en: They were friends.
sentences.zh: 他们曾是朋友。

sentences.en: It doesn't take much to inject the virus of hatred.
sentences.zh: 注入仇恨的病毒并不需要太多。

sentences.en: All it takes is for a leader to designate those former neighbors as your enemy and for somebody to start shooting.
sentences.zh: 只需要一个领导人将那些曾经的邻居指定为你的敌人，然后有人开始开枪。

sentences.en: The virus of hatred is always there just beneath the surface.
sentences.zh: 仇恨的病毒总是潜伏在表象之下。

sentences.en: There was no need for Vladimir Putin to attack Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 弗拉基米尔·普京根本没有必要攻击乌克兰。

sentences.en: It's not a country that really needs more land.
sentences.zh: 它并不是一个真正需要更多土地的国家。

sentences.en: It's by far the largest state on the face of the earth.
sentences.zh: 它是地球上迄今为止最大的国家。

sentences.en: But autocratic leaders develop obsessions.
sentences.zh: 但独裁领导人往往会产生执念。

sentences.en: Vladimir Putin developed one with Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 弗拉基米尔·普京对乌克兰就产生了这种执念。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: That's really why these institutions that have been created to make sure that international law can actually be applied to war crimes, to genocide, to crimes against humanity,
sentences.zh: 这正是为什么我们要建立这些机构，以确保国际法能够真正应用于战争罪、种族灭绝、危害人类罪，

sentences.en: that people can be held accountable.
sentences.zh: 让人们能够被追究责任。

sentences.en: That is why they are so important.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它们如此重要。

sentences.en: They're imperfect.
sentences.zh: 它们并不完美。

sentences.en: They're cumbersome.
sentences.zh: 它们很繁琐。

sentences.en: But what's the alternative?
sentences.zh: 但除此之外还有什么选择呢？

sentences.en: Those bodies lying in Bucha, they had families, right?
sentences.zh: 布查街头那些躺着的尸体，他们也有家人，对吧？

sentences.en: They had kids.
sentences.zh: 他们有孩子。

sentences.en: Some justice being brought.
sentences.zh: 实现一些正义。

sentences.en: Even if it's
sentences.zh: 哪怕是

sentences.en: 10 years down the road, that will be meaningful.
sentences.zh: 10年之后，那也是有意义的。

sentences.en: Roger, thank you.
sentences.zh: 罗杰，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。
